captures.q: What is “Enter the Crimson Hexagon — The Seat Map of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive: Method, Locations, Organization and Contents (EA-HEXAGON-ENTER-01 v1.0)” by Lee Sharks (Alexanarch deposit #1687, AXN:06FD), and how does it work? Ground your answer in the document itself.
captures.description: THE RECORD PAGE'S ASK CHATGPT LINK FOR #1687, SIGNED OUT: the composition reads the deposit's full text and carries its counts, its four sources, the room reading and its verification, the rulings, the second pass, the operative phrases, the reading protocol, the worked route from the Sappho Room to Borges, the files with their commits and hashes, and what is not yet in the map, with exact quotations throughout. It embeds two image cards from outside the archive on the route (a Medium post by Alex Skelton, 'Interpreting Sappho 31, badly', and a Conciliar Post essay on Borges's Library of Babel), drops the cause of the entrance's change (the removal of 2026-06-19 and the erratum #1426 by name), generalises one rule of the reading to every seat, and adds three disclaimers the deposit does not make.

captures.description: THE OPERATIVE PHRASE WITH A COLON, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'Enter the Crimson Hexagon is a distributed literary/digital project and epic work by Lee Sharks (2004–present), hosted through the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.' Then: 'It is accessed via its archive rather than a summarizer, meaning passages and structures change or persist depending on how they are entered.' Then the analytics company merged into Brandwatch, and Borges's 'crimson hexagon'. Five cards: Pew Research Center (Crimson Hexagon's methodology), crimsonhexagonal.org (the entrance), Literature Stack Exchange (Borges), Brandwatch, crimsonhexagonal.org (the home page).
